scienceObservations: Both languages explicitly interpret flux as a directed crossing count relative to the selected normal of the loop plane. The selected normal is a convention, not an assumed outward normal for an open surface.

Both retain the conditional density normalization on unit area perpendicular to vector B, equal to the magnitude B. This is an interpretation under a chosen field-line depiction convention, not a claim that physical lines form an intrinsic discrete count.

Positive and negative crossings are now assigned explicitly according to crossing sense relative to the normal. Along/against expresses positive/negative normal-component sense; it does not impose an extra condition that every field line be parallel to the normal.

Reversal of the selected normal reverses the directed crossing sign and flux sign while leaving the geometrical crossings fixed. This resolves the original signed-flux versus unsigned-count inconsistency without changing Phi or B_n into an absolute value.

The unsigned geometrical interpretation is explicitly restricted to the uniform-field, plane-loop case already bound by the unchanged preceding objects. In that case the crossing sense is uniform over the plane, so ignoring it yields only flux magnitude. The repair does not make an unrestricted claim for mixed-sign crossings or nonuniform fields.
No acute-angle assumption, figure-derived condition, new numerical example, task, choice or solution is needed or introduced. All three existing equalities and both equation tags remain unchanged.
